mechanism.potential: uC=(uA+uB)/2 using the two existing convolution potentials. Do not add a learned kernel or use global coordinates, source direction, labels, future data or whole-body statistics.
mechanism.response: hC=2*max(0,1-(uC-muC)^2/(9*sigmaC^2))^4-1, identical polynomial family to the existing responses, bounded[-1,1]. mu0=(muA+muB)/2; sigma0=sqrt(sigmaA*sigmaB).

parameters.latent: z=(z_mu,z_sigma); muC=mu0*exp(0.15*tanh(z_mu)); sigmaC=sigma0*exp(0.25*tanh(z_sigma)). z0=[0,0] is the fixed midpoint baseline. No clipping, wider domain or extra parameter after seeing forward results.

mechanism.selection: At ready state calculate the original choose(greedy) exactly, including original A/B heat tie-breaking and w0 tie. Select C only where scoreC=birthC-deathC is STRICTLY greater than max(scoreA,scoreB) and ready neighborhood(rho)>0. Otherwise retain the original greedy w field bit-for-bit. On C ties retain old policy. Record score/choice fields before native.
mechanism.execution: Lock the C-mask and original A/B weight before native. At the actual after-actor generation stage recompute uA/uB/uC and hC from the actual body, apply hC only at locked C sites and exact original mixed h elsewhere. Original native handles all deaths, birth admission and payments once. Do not substitute hypothetical ready births for actual births. Aggregate hypothetical scores are not an isolated per-site causal action estimate.
mechanism.fixed_baselines: Original two-response greedy; three-response with z0 fixed midpoint; always_midpoint uses hC(z0) everywhere with ready neighborhood>0 and old fallback outside, without a greedy comparison. This constant-rule baseline has identical pricing and full accounting.
mechanism.cost_scope: Existing physical cost formulas unchanged. Additional response/admit arithmetic is not physically priced; report this openly. No claim of a fully priced new biological sensing/computation channel.
mechanism.classification: Outer selection of a fixed generating rule, followed by fixed lifetime deployment. Not individual lifetime learning and not automatically a novel algorithm. Trained behavior requires a nonzero selected change and actual action differences; fixed midpoint or original fallback is not a learned success.
